steps.what: Assess the child's or disabled patient's communication, attention and access needs with the patient or carer and choose suitable special test and communication techniques.
Use and adapt the special techniques during assessment and treatment, observe the patient's actual response and decide whether the findings are reliable enough for the clinical purpose.
Write and check the actual techniques used, patient response, findings and limitations in the existing orthoptic clinical record system {OTHER}.
Save the checked final adapted-assessment note to the clinical record system {OTHER}.

tasks.enabler_now: Native clinical fields already support the record and do not create a new saving merely by running.
tasks.still_hard: Distress, limited communication and variable responses require immediate clinical adaptation.
tasks.human_edge: Build trust and recognise when the test result is unreliable despite apparent cooperation.

assumptions: This is the use-and-adapt instance of the task, through its existing clinical note. It does not include a separate research project developing a new validated test. Shares are illustrative, not measured.

steps.what: Select the clinical method and teaching examples for students, resident physicians or other health professionals; configure native {DOCS} exercise layouts and approved method-section references, then check the completed material.
Teach and demonstrate the clinical method, supervise practice and discuss interpretation and limitations; observe the learner's actual performance.
Write and check the actual attendance, method covered, observed learning and follow-up in the existing {LMS} teaching record.
Save the checked final teaching record in {LMS}, preserving the distinction between attendance and any separate competence authorisation.

tasks.design: Reuse native exercise layouts and approved method references in {DOCS}. The orthoptist chooses and checks the clinical content, teaches the learners and records actual delivery in {LMS}; no tool decides clinical competence.

tasks.human_edge: Recognise a misunderstanding before it becomes an unsafe clinical habit.

evidence.claim: Native document templates can reuse approved clinical teaching sections without evaluating learners.

Native templates are tried before code. Only layout and repeated references lose time; clinical selection, final material checks, actual teaching and record writing retain effort. Examples are already cleared for teaching; no free anonymisation work is assumed.

steps.what: Review the relevant eye-care findings and current questions for collaboration with ophthalmologists, optometrists or other specialists, including glaucoma, cataract or retinal-disease context where relevant.
Discuss diagnosis, treatment or management with the relevant specialists, explain orthoptic findings and agree responsibilities within each professional's existing scope.
Write and check the actual specialist discussion, agreed responsibilities and unresolved questions in the existing clinical record system {OTHER}.
Save the checked final collaboration note in the clinical record system {OTHER}.

tasks.design: Retain direct specialist discussion and its existing native clinical note in {OTHER}. Review, conversation, actual note writing and save are explicit; this scenario has no supported additional labour-saving mechanism after considering each separately.
tasks.previous_blocker: The work depends on reconciling clinical interpretations and responsibilities, not routing a standard message.

tasks.still_hard: Complex eye disease and conflicting findings need specialist dialogue and judgement.
tasks.human_edge: Explain what the orthoptic findings do and do not establish, and resolve who will act.

tasks.short: Prepare a diagnostic or treatment report

steps.what: Verify the report's purpose, patient and recipient, then read the actual orthoptic findings, diagnosis and treatment decisions in the clinical record system {OTHER}.
Populate the report's patient, encounter and selected test-result fields using native report configuration in the clinical record system {OTHER}; check dates, laterality, units and source references.

Draft the report narrative for the medical practitioner or therapist from the verified source pack; where native sections cannot express the existing findings, use one bounded draft proposal and check every clinical statement against its source.
outputs: source-checked draft diagnostic or treatment report

loop.purpose: Express already recorded orthoptic findings and care decisions in a recipient-appropriate draft without adding clinical advice.
loop.input: Verified source passages with record IDs, structured result fields and the report purpose.
loop.output: Draft narrative with a source reference for each clinical statement and explicit unresolved gaps.
loop.check: The orthoptist compares every statement with the original record for laterality, values, dates, negation, uncertainty, diagnosis, treatment and follow-up meaning; rejects omissions, altered emphasis and unsupported recommendations.
loop.stop: One draft and at most one correction, then manual completion. Missing or conflicting clinical sources stop automatic drafting; no record write or send is allowed.
loop.why_not_simpler: Native report sections and exact field reuse come first. Only variable prose connecting existing findings to the recipient's question needs the bounded draft.

steps.what: Review and correct the complete diagnostic or treatment report as a whole, ensuring it accurately conveys the clinical limits and required follow-up; approve the final version and intended recipient.
inputs: source-checked draft diagnostic or treatment report
outputs: checked final diagnostic or treatment report

steps.what: Save the checked final diagnostic or treatment report in the clinical record system {OTHER}.
inputs: checked final diagnostic or treatment report

steps.what: Send the exact stored report to the checked medical practitioner or therapist through the existing secure clinical exchange in {OTHER}.

tasks.design: Use native report fields in the clinical record system {OTHER} first, then a bounded narrative draft only for the remaining variable prose. The orthoptist checks every clinical statement against the record and reviews the completed report before separate save and secure-send actions.
tasks.previous_blocker: Existing clinical findings were repeatedly retyped and connected into recipient-specific prose.
tasks.enabler_now: Native fields can carry results and source references; a constrained draft can propose wording from supplied passages.
tasks.still_hard: Laterality, uncertainty and clinically significant omissions need a clinician who understands the encounter.
tasks.human_edge: Ensure the report communicates the clinical meaning and limitations of the actual findings.

ambition.what: No new diagnosis, treatment or disclosure authority.

tasks.altitude: Less repeated report drafting; full responsibility for the clinical report remains.

reach.learn: Encounter references and clinical document versions.

evidence.claim: A bounded text model can propose prose from supplied clinical notes but requires source-based checking for omissions and altered meaning.

assumptions: Boundary starts with completed clinical findings and care decisions and ends at report delivery. It does not create a new diagnosis or repeat the underlying examination or specialist collaboration. Shares are a scenario, not measured savings.

Existing clinicians produce patient and encounter IDs, test date, test name, value, unit, laterality, findings, diagnosis, treatment and follow-up decisions. The orthoptist verifies source passages and recipient in s1-s2. Manual entry and source checking remain counted; absent or conflicting fields trigger manual drafting, not inference.

Native report templates are tested before a model. A permitted deployment must keep patient information within existing authorised clinical processing and access arrangements; availability and deployment requirements are customer unknowns. No ambient recording or extra patient-data collection is assumed.

All semantic checking is retained in s3 and final clinical review in s4. The final report exists before approval; changes void both s5 and s6 approvals. Save and send retain their full ordinary one-hour shares.
unknowns: Permitted clinical drafting deployment and access
research_questions: Do source-linked drafts reduce total report time after laterality, omission and uncertainty checks?

already_counted.description: Check native report fields and every drafted clinical statement against the record.

incremental.description: Maintain report mappings and review draft behaviour for clinical omissions after changes.

approvals.approved_version: Completed final diagnostic or treatment report checked at the end of s4
Same final report snapshot and recipient checked at the end of s4, unchanged by s5

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Native fields save 10 hours and source-checked prose drafting 12.25 hours per 100 baseline hours, less 3 upkeep: 19.25 net. Zero if native reports already suffice or draft correction removes the gain. Source review, final clinical review, save and send retain their stated time.
